title: [RFE] Allow importing a RKE2 cluster without immediately upgrading it
body: We manage clusters in Rancher for which we do not have operational responsibility, so we should never initiate a version upgrade. Importing an existing RKE2 cluster should only import it, but Rancher automatically starts upgrading it without offering a way to cancel. I would like upgrades of imported clusters to be optional instead of mandatory.

symptoms_visible: When I import an existing RKE2 cluster, Rancher immediately starts an upgrade instead of only importing it.
N0.label: N0 automatic upgrade reported

symptoms_visible: The upgrade job could not pull its image because the cluster is partially air-gapped, and the cluster still reports that a worker is being upgraded.
The downstream cluster has rke2-master-plan and rke2-worker-plan objects for its current RKE2 version.
N1.label: N1 failed upgrade state documented

symptoms_visible: After I imported another cluster, it immediately entered 'Upgrading' and the UI began switching between 'Active' and 'Upgrading'.
The management logs repeatedly compare cluster versions such as v1.27.12+rke2r1 with node versions such as v1.27.12 and say the cluster is being upgraded.
N2.label: N2 reproduction and raw version comparison collected

symptoms_visible: After I delete the upgrade plans, they reappear a few minutes later and the cluster keeps switching between 'Active' and 'Upgrading'.
Removing the node plan annotation or editing the cluster status is temporary because Rancher writes the values back.
N2_x.label: N2_x manual cleanup aftermath

symptoms_visible: The imported cluster contains Windows nodes, and Rancher continues to alternate its status between 'Active' and 'Upgrading'.
N3.label: N3 Windows-node trigger established

symptoms_visible: After I disable the managed-system-upgrade-controller feature flag, remove the cluster, and import it again, the new cluster still goes straight into 'Upgrading'.
I no longer see upgrade plan objects or an upgrade waiting to run, but the 'cluster is being upgraded' condition returns whenever I delete it.
N3_x.label: N3_x unrelated feature flag aftermath

symptoms_visible: After updating Rancher to a build containing the fixes, the imported clusters no longer start unwanted upgrades or alternate between 'Active' and 'Upgrading'.
N_terminal.label: terminal reporter-confirmed resolution

question_patterns: Can you describe exactly what happened during the import and what upgrade activity you observed?
What upgrade workload was created, and what happened to it?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Rancher started a Kubernetes upgrade job. It hung because this cluster is partially air-gapped and could not pull the required image. I deleted the job, including some retries, but the cluster still says it is being upgraded.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: No upgrade job or plan was created; only the UI label changed briefly and then returned to Active.
The upgrade job failed for a registry authentication error rather than because the cluster is air-gapped.

question_patterns: What does the Upgraded condition on the provisioning cluster object currently say?
Can you paste the condition responsible for the upgrade status?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The condition has type Upgraded, status Unknown, and the message says 'worker node [supercluster-node1] being upgraded'.

question_patterns: Can you share the sanitized <redacted-host> YAML and list any <redacted-host> objects on the imported cluster?
Are system-upgrade-controller plan objects still present downstream?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I pasted the provisioning Cluster YAML. On the imported cluster, cattle-system contains rke2-master-plan and rke2-worker-plan objects using rancher/rke2-upgrade, both targeting v1.30.5+rke2r1.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: There are no upgrade plan objects, and the provisioning Cluster has no Upgraded condition.

edges.comment: Reporter c1, c3 and c4: the original reporter describes the failed air-gapped upgrade, supplies the screenshot, provisioning Cluster YAML, condition, and downstream plan listing. Deleting the jobs was a persistent emergency intervention, so the destination uses S1b.

question_patterns: Can you enable debug logging on the Rancher management pods, import another affected cluster, and report what happens?
Please reproduce the import with Rancher debug logging enabled and share the relevant raw output.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I upgraded Rancher, enabled debug logging on the management cluster, and imported another external cluster. It immediately went into 'cluster is being upgraded', and the GUI began switching between Active and Upgrading every second or so.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: With debug logging enabled, the new cluster imported as Active and no upgrade status or workload appeared.
The status switches every few seconds rather than every second.

question_patterns: What are the relevant k3s-based-upgrader lines in the management-cluster debug log?
Please paste the raw version values printed when the controller decides to upgrade.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The log repeatedly says things like: cluster version [v1.27.12+rke2r1] is newer than observed node version [v1.27.12], followed by 'upgrading cluster ... because cluster version ... is newer than observed node version'. It prints the same pattern for v1.30.5+rke2r1 compared with v1.30.5.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The logs compare two genuinely different Kubernetes minor versions, such as cluster v1.30 with nodes on v1.29.
The same base-version mismatch appears for different cluster and machine identifiers.

question_patterns: What versions do kubectl and the cluster objects report for the individual nodes?
Do all nodes include the same RKE2 suffix in their version strings?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Some nodes report v1.27.12 with no suffix, while the control-plane nodes report values such as v1.27.12+rke2r1. One control-plane node also reports v1.26.14+rke2r1. I don't know whether those different formats are confusing Rancher.

edges.comment: Reporter c6-c9: participant1 requested a debug-enabled import; the same reporter imported and kept another cluster, making this S2. The answers preserve the raw controller messages and version strings without putting the Windows-node diagnosis into the reporter's mouth.

solution.intent: Manually clear the stuck upgrade state by deleting downstream upgrade plans and controller artifacts, removing plan annotations, and editing the Upgraded condition.
solution.concrete_example: Delete rke2-master-plan and rke2-worker-plan downstream, remove the <redacted-host> annotation from nodes, and set the provisioning Cluster's Upgraded condition to True with an empty message.

edges.comment: Participant1 c2 suggested condition and plan cleanup; reporter c7-c9 tried deleting plans, removing a node annotation, and editing status. The plans or status returned and the UI kept flapping, so this is a falsified persistent intervention on the reporter's clusters.

question_patterns: Do these imported clusters contain any Windows nodes?
Are the nodes that omit the RKE2 version metadata Windows nodes?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes, this cluster has Windows nodes. I should have included that in the original description.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: No, every node is Linux and all of them are standard supported RKE2 nodes.
Only one worker is Windows; the rest are Linux nodes.

edges.comment: Participant1 c13 explicitly asks whether the affected cluster contains Windows nodes; the original reporter confirms this in c14. This is the decisive must-ask fact that allows the maintainer to connect the raw version mismatch to the accepted diagnosis.

solution.intent: Disable the managed-system-upgrade-controller feature flag and reimport the cluster to prevent Rancher from initiating or displaying an upgrade.
solution.concrete_example: Set CATTLE_FEATURES:managed-system-upgrade-controller=false on the Rancher server pods, remove the affected imported cluster, and add it again.

edges.comment: Reporter c18 independently tried this persistent configuration change and reimport. Participant1 c19 explains that the flag controls migration of the system-upgrade-controller installation mechanism, not whether Rancher manages imported-cluster versions; the reimport still showed Upgrading.

solution.intent: Update Rancher to a build containing both the Windows-node upgrade-detection fix and the option to disable Kubernetes version management for imported RKE2/K3s clusters; use the opt-out for clusters Rancher must not upgrade, then have the operator verify the imported clusters remain stable.
solution.concrete_example: Move to the Rancher release containing the Windows-node handling fix and imported-cluster version-management control. Disable version management for provider-managed imports, then confirm that an affected cluster remains Active without plans or an Upgraded condition being recreated. The reporter later confirmed that after moving to Rancher 2.11 all of the reported problems were gone.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied raw logs comparing v1.27.12+rke2r1 with v1.27.12 and later confirmed Windows nodes. The maintainer inferred that Windows nodes omit the metadata component, connected the behavior to the existing Windows-node bug, and clarified that the feature flag only controls controller-installation migration rather than version management.

edges.comment: Participant1 c15, c19 and c21 identifies the Windows-node bug and the separate imported-cluster version-management opt-out as the combined resolution. Reporter c22 later verifies on their own deployment that after updating to 2.11 all problems are gone.

solution.intent: Update Rancher to a build containing the Windows-node upgrade-detection fix and the imported-cluster version-management opt-out, instead of attempting manual cleanup or using an unrelated feature flag; then verify the affected imports remain stable.
solution.concrete_example: Install the Rancher build with corrected Windows-node handling and the ability to opt imported RKE2/K3s clusters out of Kubernetes version management. Enable that opt-out for these provider-managed clusters and verify that their status remains Active. The reporter ultimately confirmed the problem was gone after updating to Rancher 2.11.
solution.inference_hint: The engineer must interpret the raw version comparison together with the confirmed Windows nodes. The accepted diagnosis is that Windows nodes report versions without the RKE2 metadata suffix and are incorrectly treated as older, not that a real Kubernetes version difference necessarily requires an upgrade.

edges.comment: Shortcut answer available as soon as c14 establishes Windows nodes. It skips the reporter's later unsuccessful feature-flag experiment while preserving the same accepted technical resolution and eventual reporter verification.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: Windows nodes can report Kubernetes versions without the RKE2 metadata suffix, causing Rancher's imported-cluster upgrader to compare values such as v1.27.12+rke2r1 and v1.27.12 and falsely decide that an upgrade is required.
Diagnosis must be grounded in the management-controller debug output, the mixed node version strings, and confirmation that the affected clusters contain Windows nodes.

Must recommend a Rancher build containing corrected Windows-node upgrade detection and the ability to disable Kubernetes version management for imported RKE2/K3s clusters, using that opt-out for clusters the operator is not permitted to upgrade.

Must not present deleting upgrade plans, removing node annotations, or editing cluster status as a durable fix; those objects or conditions were recreated and the UI continued switching between Active and Upgrading.

Must not claim that disabling the managed-system-upgrade-controller feature flag disables imported-cluster version upgrades; the reporter tried it and the maintainer clarified that it controls installation-mechanism migration instead.

Must ask the reporter to verify the affected imported clusters on a build containing the fixes and declare resolution only after the reporter confirms the unwanted upgrade behavior and status flapping are gone.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced Kubernetes and Rancher operator who can inspect custom resources, plans, node annotations, Helm environment variables, and management-pod debug logs, but does not control the service provider's cluster provisioning and is contractually prohibited from performing node upgrades.
persona_hint.communication_style: Detailed, candid, and cooperative; pastes YAML and logs, carefully explains operational constraints, asks before making risky changes, and becomes visibly concerned when automated actions cannot be stopped.
